title: Connect
subtitle: Find people, expertise, and opportunities for what you are building right now.
investmentNotice: The Connect supports introductions. It does not broker investments or provide investment advice.

filters.search: Search titles, descriptions, topics and industries

empty.title: No listing currently meets every selected criterion.
empty.text: Reset the filters or make your own current need or contribution concrete.
empty.firstText: Connect only works once someone starts. Say what you are looking for or what you can contribute – that becomes the first entry others see.

form.direction: What would you like to do?
form.title: Short title
form.summaryHint: Be specific about the need or offer and what would make a useful connection.
form.topicsHint: Separate with commas, up to {max}. E.g. B2B sales, product strategy, software development, fundraising.
form.industriesHint: Separate with commas, up to {max}. E.g. HealthTech, SaaS, ClimateTech, Future of Work.
form.locationsHint: Separate with commas, up to {max}. E.g. Berlin, Brandenburg.
form.scopeHint: Describes geographic relevance independently of remote work.
form.startsOnHint: Optional. When does the content become relevant?
form.endsOnHint: Optional. With no end date, the timeframe remains flexible.

visibility.profilePublicHint: Your published Connect profile can be opened without signing in and found by search engines.

visibility.listingConfirm: I want to publish this listing publicly with these details.

create.kindText: Choose a category. Co-Founder search remains a dedicated, deeper workflow.
create.profileRequiredText: You can save this listing as a draft at any time. It can only be published once your Connect profile is active – otherwise nobody can see who the offer comes from.

cofounder.title: Co-Founder search
cofounder.text: Co-Founder search has its own area. It lets you consider experience and practical constraints alongside expectations about working together.
cofounder.cta: Set up or view Co-Founder search

detail.what: What is being sought or offered?

public.aboutText: CoFoundery Connect makes concrete needs and offers around startups and entrepreneurship visible. Contact requests remain tied to a listing and protected CoFoundery access.
public.contactRequiresAccess: You need CoFoundery access to get in touch. New access continues to follow the controlled beta contract.

contact.title: Contacts
contact.text: Review requests and continue accepted contacts in a private internal exchange.
contact.messageLabel: Why would you like to get in touch?
contact.messageHint: Briefly explain what you would like to discuss and why an exchange could be useful. 10–500 characters.
contact.error: The contact request could not be updated.

statusText.pending: The recipient will decide about your request.
statusText.accepted: You both agreed to get in touch and can continue the exchange here.

contact.profileRequiredText: Before you message someone, the other side needs something to look at. Create your Connect profile and publish it – you will come back here afterwards.
contact.personMessageHint: Without a listing there is no occasion the other person can read along. So say briefly why you are getting in touch and what you have in mind – it saves a round trip.
contact.personProfileRequiredText: Writing to others requires a published profile of your own. Not a hurdle but mutuality: whoever is written to should be able to see who is writing.

messages.emptyText: You have accepted the contact. Write a first message when you would like to start the exchange.
messages.error: The message could not be sent. Please check the text.
messages.counterpartGoneText: Your history stays with you – you can read back what was written. Replying is no longer possible; there would be nobody to read it.
messages.inboxText: All your conversations in one place – from Connect and from Find. Each one says where it came from.
messages.inboxEmptyText: Once a contact request is accepted, you respond to something unsolved, or an intro in Find is agreed, you'll find the conversation here.

my.title: My connect listings
my.expiresIn: Expires in {days} days – after that it is no longer visible to others.
my.problemsEmpty: You have not described anything yet.

profile.title: Your Connect profile
profile.text: You explicitly choose the compact identity other members can see. Private profile, Discovery, and assessment data remain separate.
profile.name: Display name
profile.headline: Headline
profile.rolesHint: These roles only describe you in the Connect and never change permissions.
profile.consent: “Publish Connect profile” publishes your profile with the selected visibility. Listings have independent visibility; messages remain private.

photo.title: Profile photo
photo.helper: Your profile photo appears inside CoFoundery on your Connect profile and Connect listings.

profile.identityText: You maintain these details in one place in your profile. Changes there appear here immediately.
profile.identityMissing: Nothing entered yet. Without a name, a headline and a text about you, your Connect profile cannot be published.
profile.reachHint: Optional. The value often lies one step out – who you know sometimes helps more than what you can do yourself.
profile.reachPlaceholder: e.g. I know a lot of managers in outpatient care and a few people in health insurance administration.
profile.openToHint: A first message rarely fails on the topic and often on the question of what form is appropriate. Take that hurdle away.
profile.contactNoteTitle: How do people reach you best?
profile.contactNoteHint: One sentence. Whatever the options above do not cover – times, preferences, what you want to know upfront.
profile.contactNotePlaceholder: e.g. Write me a short note about what it is about – I usually reply within two days.
profile.membersOnlyNote: These three entries are only visible to signed-in members – they do not appear on your public page.
profile.reachNoNames: Please no names: this is about what kind of people you know, not which ones. They have not agreed to appear here.
profile.suggestableLabel: I would like to be suggested to others
profile.suggestableHint: People whose fields or industries overlap with yours will occasionally see your profile under “For you” – at most three suggestions a week, and only inside the platform.
profile.suggestableOffHint: Switched off you stay findable as usual: in the people list, through search and through your entries. You simply won't be suggested to anyone.

problems.title: What people see unsolved
problems.text: This is what people experience as unsolved around them. Some want to build something from it, some already are, and some simply describe it because someone ought to know.
problems.createTitle: What do you see that ought to be solved?
problems.createText: Describe it concretely enough that someone without your background understands it – who it affects, and what is missing today.
problems.searchPlaceholder: Search titles, descriptions, topics and places
problems.interestCount: {count, plural, =0 {Nobody would work on it yet} one {1 person would work on it} other {# people would work on it}}
problems.emptyFirstText: The first problem is the hardest. Describe something you notice around you – even if you have no solution for it.
problems.emptyFilteredText: Reset the filters, or describe what you notice yourself.

intentHints.observation: I am describing it because someone ought to know. I have no plans with it myself.
intentHints.wants_to_build: I would build something from this and am looking for people to found with.
intentHints.already_building: I am already working on a solution – so nobody starts the same thing independently.

statuses.draft: Not published yet. Only you can see this.

form.title: What is it about, in one sentence?
form.titlePlaceholder: For example: Care services cannot find short-notice cover
form.titleHint: This sentence appears in the overview later.
form.descriptionPlaceholder: For example: When someone drops out at short notice, managers spend hours phoning down lists. There is no shared overview of who could step in when.
form.descriptionHint: At least {min} characters. Who does it affect, how often, and what happens instead today?
form.intent: What do you intend with this?
form.intentHint: This decides what others can expect from you – and whether they approach you.

problems.profileRequiredText: You can save a draft at any time. A problem can only be published once your Connect profile is active – otherwise nobody can respond to it.
problems.ownText: Withdrawing hides it from others. Marking it solved leaves it standing but ends the search.
problems.interestedEmpty: Nobody yet. That says little – a problem usually takes a while before someone comes across it.
problems.interestText: Say briefly what you bring or why this concerns you. The person who posted it then decides whether to start a conversation.
problems.interestNotePlaceholder: For example: I have worked in this field for years and know the processes from the inside.
problems.interestNoteHint: At least {min} characters. A click without words helps nobody.
problems.interestSaved: Your response has arrived. If the person who posted it starts a conversation, you will find it under Messages.
problems.yourInterestText: Only the person who posted it sees your name. For everyone else, only the number counts.
problems.withdrawInterestQuestion: Really withdraw? A conversation that came from it will disappear too.
problems.interestProfileRequiredText: Before you get in touch, the other side needs something to look at. Create your Connect profile – you will come back here afterwards.
problems.editText: Changes are visible immediately. Anyone who already expressed interest stays.
problems.usageTitle: How a business idea comes out of this
problems.usageLead: Most companies do not start with an idea. They start with a problem someone knows up close and nobody solves. Those are what stand here – before anyone turned them into an idea.

usageWays.read: Read, if you want to found something but do not yet know what. These are observations from people working in the field – not a list of trends.
usageWays.join: Join in, if one of them concerns you. Say what you bring; the person who posted decides whether it becomes a conversation.
usageWays.write: Describe one yourself, even with no intention of your own. What you have noticed for years may be someone else's beginning.

problems.usageCaveatTitle: And what this does not do
problems.usageCaveat: Not every problem becomes a business. Whether anyone would pay for a solution, whether it adds up, whether it already exists – this board answers none of that. It only makes sure you ask the question about something real rather than a hunch.
problems.usageNext: If one of them stays with you: describe it from your own side, or get in touch with the person who posted it.
problems.confirmText: A problem several people recognise is different from one person's annoyance. Say briefly how you know it – nothing more comes of it.
problems.confirmPrivacy: Nobody learns that it was you – not even the person who posted. Only the numbers are visible.
problems.confirmationsEmpty: Nobody has confirmed this yet. That says little – most problems take a while before someone comes across them.
problems.confirmationsCount: {count, plural, =0 {Nobody has confirmed this yet} one {1 person knows this too} other {# people know this too}}
problems.approachesTitle: How one would go about it
problems.approachesText: Several approaches stand here side by side, in no order. That is deliberate: two people should see whether they would build the same thing – before they found together, not after.
problems.approachesEmpty: Nobody has described how they would go about this. You could write the first view on it.
problems.approachFormTitle: How would you go about it?
problems.approachFormText: Three fields, not a business plan. Whether anyone would pay for it is still not what this board answers – but the approach makes visible what you would have to talk about.
problems.approachSummaryPlaceholder: For example: a shared availability list for several services in a region, which carers fill in themselves when they could step in.
problems.approachAudiencePlaceholder: For example: outpatient services with ten to fifty employees
problems.approachNeeds: What would you need for it?
problems.approachNeedsPlaceholder: For example: someone who knows how care work runs from the inside.
problems.approachNeedsHint: Better concrete than a job title.
problems.approachSaved: Your approach now stands with the problem.
problems.yourApproachWithdrawn: Withdrawn. Only you still see it – saving again puts it back.
problems.withdrawApproachQuestion: Really withdraw the approach? Your text stays with you.
problems.approachProfileRequiredText: An approach is public and carries your name. Create your Connect profile – you will come back here afterwards.
problems.approachReplyTitle: Get in touch about this approach
problems.approachReplyText: Say briefly what interests you about it or what you would contribute. That person then decides whether it becomes a conversation.
problems.approachReplyPlaceholder: For example: I have built exactly this for a different field and would like to talk about it.
problems.approachInterestSaved: Your message has arrived. If that person starts a conversation, you will find it under Messages.
problems.approachRepliesTitle: Who got in touch about your approach
problems.approachRepliesEmpty: Nobody yet. An approach usually takes a while before someone comes across it.
problems.approachReplyProfileRequiredText: Before you get in touch, the other side needs something to look at. Create your Connect profile – you will come back here afterwards.
problems.publicJoinText: Inside you can see who else knows this problem and how others would approach it. That needs an account.
problems.visibilityPublicHint: The page is then reachable without an account and may appear on Google.
problems.visibilityPreviewItems: Your title, your description, topics, places and your name. Not out there: other people's approaches, the confirmations, and who got in touch – we have no consent from those people for that.
problems.visibilityConfirm: I understand that this text will then be publicly readable – including by people from my professional environment – and that I can take it back at any time.
problems.visibilityCaution: Think for a moment before you do: a description from your working day often says something about your employer too.
problems.orphanNotice: This person deleted their account and left the text standing anonymously. The problem can no longer be changed, and a message here would reach nobody.
problems.outlivesLabel: May stay anonymously if I delete my account
problems.outlivesHint: Without this, the problem disappears with your account – and with it the approaches others wrote for it. With it, the text stays without your name. You will be asked again when you delete.
problems.outlivesApproachLabel: May stay anonymously if I delete my account
problems.outlivesApproachHint: This approach sits on someone else's page. Without this, it disappears from there along with your account.

searches.title: Saved searches
searches.text: What you saved you do not have to enter again – and when something new matches, we let you know.
searches.saveText: We will tell you about new entries and descriptions that meet all of your criteria.
searches.emptyText: Narrow down what you are looking for in the overview and save it. After that you do not have to keep checking yourself.

saved.created: Search saved. From now on we will tell you what matches.

searches.capabilitiesText: Only entries from people who have disclosed at least one of these areas will trigger a notification. Anyone keeping their capabilities private never shows up here.

ventures.title: What you have built
ventures.text: Up to five companies, projects or activities. They sit with your profile – whoever finds you sees where you come from.
ventures.emptyText: Add what you are working on. The audience matters most: it lets someone reading recognise whether they know a person this would suit.
ventures.name: Name
ventures.roleLabelPlaceholder: e.g. Founder · On the side since 2019 · Coach
ventures.roleLabelHint: Optional. Reality rarely fits a dropdown.
ventures.whatItDoesPlaceholder: Describe what you do and what is different about it. At least 50 characters.
ventures.audiencePlaceholder: e.g. Self-employed midwives with no time for marketing
ventures.audienceHint: The most important field. It lets someone reading recognise whether they know a person this would suit – and pass you on.
ventures.motivationPlaceholder: e.g. I have seen how much good work stays invisible simply because nobody has time to show it.
ventures.motivationHint: Optional – and often the part that sticks. Values usually only come up in the third conversation.
ventures.websiteHint: The address of your website. You can paste it from the address bar – we'll add the “https://”. Links always open a new window.
ventures.logoHint: Optional, 2 MB maximum. JPG, PNG or WebP.
ventures.hiddenNote: Hidden. Only you see this entry.
ventures.deleteQuestion: Really delete this entry? This cannot be undone.
ventures.limitReached: Five entries is the maximum. Delete or hide one to make room.

ventures.profileLinkHint: Up to five entries that sit with your profile.
ventures.openLinkHint: Opens the website in a new window
ventures.directoryText: What the people here are working on. Every entry shows who is behind it – one click takes you to them.

resources.title: Access and networks
resources.text: From your published listings, a language model reads out which doors you can open – people you know, places you can reach, things you can offer. Every suggestion shows the passage it rests on. None of it counts before you agree.
resources.privateNote: So far this is visible only to you. Whether and where it ever appears in your profile is a decision you make explicitly, later.

highlight.title: From the network
highlight.randomNote: Picked at random, changes on every visit

suggestions.title: For you
suggestions.text: From what you wrote yourself – fields and industries in your profile, your requests, and the problems you named – we look for offers, companies, people and unsolved problems that overlap. Every suggestion shows you the word that triggered it.
suggestions.emptyText: We only suggest what overlaps with your own entries – rather nothing than something arbitrary. The more precise your profile is, and above all: the sooner you write down what you are looking for, the more turns up.
suggestions.note: At most three suggestions a week, and they stay in the platform – none of this goes out by email. We do not suggest requests: whoever is looking for something should decide for themselves whom to approach.
